title: The Bottle Neck
summary: In a poor attic window hung the broken neck of a wine bottle, serving as a modest drinking cup for a caged linnet....
full_text:
In a poor attic window hung the broken neck of a wine bottle, serving as a modest drinking cup for a caged linnet.

That same bottle had once been filled with sparkling vintage wine, uncorked at the joyous betrothal of a handsome young sailor and his sweet bride! The sailor had tossed the empty bottle into the sea, where it drifted across stormy oceans, was shattered on rocks, and ended up as a broken neck in a junk shop.

And who owned the singing bird and the attic window? The very same bride, now an old, silver-haired maiden, who tenderly poured water into the glass cup, unaware that she was being served by the very bottle from her happiest day of youth.
moral: The fragments of past joy can still serve a humble, loving purpose in the twilight of life.
